audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 reads right: Veigar bullies a helpless pre-6 Kassadin, and the danger is entirely in mismanaging the lead — his Riftwalk all-in punishes every positional error. WR 51.08 over 1388 games supports a slight Veigar edge.
Spikes present: Veigar's 3-5 denial phase, level 6 cage-vs-Riftwalk, first-item one-shot window, late cage-neutralised scaling. All four content spikes exist and are grounded.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart carried 'Skill' on rows 0-4 and 'Kassadin' on rows 5-6 while content win[] and the packet chart both say Veigar on all seven; breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; enemyWin was a name-swap template; two copy-paste-bleed bullets; the Nether Blade auto-reset tell was unmentioned.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 — chasing is futile, caging the landing is the counter. Null Sphere (9s) shields magic damage, so poke lands hardest right after he spends it. His combo opens with the Nether Blade (W, 7s) auto reset — the wind-up is the step-back cue.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides moved to Veigar with rating and why rewrites grounded in the cage-vs-Riftwalk interaction (win[] already agrees — side-only per the chart rule); cooldowns rewritten with 5s/2s, 9s and 20s; enemyWin grounded; bleed bullets replaced with the R-stack mana fact and the W reset tell.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by surviving to items, then Riftwalking onto you with Nether Blade burst faster than your cage answers.

edits.before: Q through two units on every last-hit — each stack is permanent AP; the lane is a savings account from level 1.
edits.after: Kassadin cannot trade at level 1 — Q through him and the wave every cast; each stack is permanent AP he pays for.

edits.before: W on cage-stunned or rooted targets only — uncaged Dark Matter is a donation to his dodge stats.
edits.after: W on cage-stunned targets only — but poke freely: his one answer is a Q magic shield on a 9s cooldown.

edits.before: Cage online: drop it ON yourself when he engages, behind him when he farms — the geometry does the fighting.
edits.after: Cage online: lock his step-ups and Q-W him off every last-hit — pre-6 he has no tool to punish the bully.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown and double-stack off cannon waves. The curve is the matchup.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown, deny his CS, and bank the lead before Riftwalk arrives at 6.

edits.before: Primordial Burst online — anyone under half is now a math problem with one answer. Count R damage out loud.
edits.after: Primordial Burst online — and your cage stuns his Riftwalk landing, so his level 6 spike walks into a wall.

edits.before: Luden's spike: cage-W-Q-R deletes squishies who touch the wall. Your zone is a courtroom now.
edits.after: Luden's spike: cage the blink, W-Q-R the stun — your combo deletes him before his items arrive.

edits.before: Late Veigar IS the scaling argument: cage the choke, burst the carry, and let infinite AP write the closing statement.
edits.after: Late Veigar IS the scaling argument: cage his blink, burst him from execute range — the curve outbids his R stacks.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Check it before every step-up. - E Event Horizon (self-cage) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s at rank 3 — never chase; cage the landing instead. - Null Sphere (9s) shields magic damage: poke right after he spends it. - Your Event Horizon is 20s early; it is the lifeline — chip damage never gets it.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: His combo opens with the Nether Blade auto reset — the wind-up, not the cast, is your cue to step back; at half HP that step is your life.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: Cage him as he walks up, W the edge-stun, Q plus an auto, then out — a half-bar trade and three stacks into the bank.

notes: Chart: content win[] and the packet chart both say Veigar on all 7 rows; full carried Skill (0-4) and Kassadin (5-6). Moved full to agree per the chart rule with grounded whys — the cage-stops-Riftwalk interaction carries the late rows, and the content whys/spikes already argue it. Flagging confidence Medium on rows 5-6: conventional wisdom has Kassadin outscaling, but both data layers and the packet disagree with that here and the layers must agree; if the user wants the late rows Kassadin-sided, both layers and the whys should flip together in a follow-up. The brief's missingInteractions claims Null Sphere is 'a channel your E cancels' — Riot's text says Q INTERRUPTS channels, not that it is one, and the kit's channel flag looks like a tooltip-parse misfire; did not write that claim.
